crises.name: Brazil 2021
crises.summary: Worst inflows in the 91-year record (1931-2021). Handled with costly thermal power, imports and a new tariff surcharge, not rationing.

official_warning.what: National weather system issues a water-emergency alert for the Parana basin, June to September

onset.what: Regulator Aneel sets the red level 2 tariff flag

crises.peak: Southeast/Centre-West reservoirs bottom at 16.5% on 6 Oct 2021
costs: New 'water scarcity' tariff flag R$14.20 per 100 kWh, 49.6% above the previous top flag; average bill up about 6.8% [P]
Crisis cost estimated at R$13.8 billion [N, Agencia Brasil]

events.text: Red level 2 tariff flag for June
'Water scarcity' tariff flag starts, valid to Apr 2022

crises.name: Sichuan 2022
crises.enso: La Nina year; record heatwave and drought
crises.summary: A record heatwave and drought more than halved hydro output in a province that gets about 82% of its power from hydro. Factories were ordered to stop.

onset.what: Industrial power cut in 19 of 21 cities from 15 Aug, extended to 25 Aug

crises.peak: Hydro output down by more than half (State Grid Sichuan); rainfall 60% below normal in August
costs: Toyota and CATL plants shut [N, Bloomberg]
No official provincial cost estimate found

crises.name: Northern Vietnam 2023
crises.summary: Heat and drought cut northern hydro while demand peaked. Rolling cuts hit factories for about a month.

official_warning.what: EVN tells the industry ministry of a 'high risk of serious shortage'

onset.what: Rolling power cuts in the north (late May; exact first day not published)

crises.peak: 5.4 GW peak deficit; about 900 GWh unserved, May to June
costs: About $1.4 billion, roughly 0.3% of GDP (World Bank preliminary estimate) [P]
Firms reported revenue losses of up to 10% [P]

crises.name: Ecuador 2023-24
crises.enso: Wave 1 El Nino; late-2024 wave ENSO-neutral
crises.summary: Three waves of cuts. The grid operator warned repeatedly; the worst came in late 2024 with 14 hours a day without power.

official_warning.what: Grid operator CENACE asks for rationing; in Dec 2023 it warns of blackouts in the 2024-25 dry seasons

onset.what: Cuts of 3-4 hours a day begin

crises.peak: 14 hours a day from 24 Oct 2024; deficit up to about 1,700 MW
costs: About 1-1.5% of GDP (Finance Minister Juan Carlos Vega) [N reporting official]
About $12 million per hour of national blackout (Guayaquil Chamber of Commerce) [N]

events.text: CENACE warns of blackouts in 2024-25 dry seasons (Dec 2023)
Cuts raised to 14 hours a day

crises.name: Lake Kariba 2024
crises.summary: El Nino drained the world's largest man-made reservoir. Zambia, which gets about 86% of its power from hydro, cut power for most of the day.

official_warning.what: Zambezi River Authority cuts the 2024 water allocation from 30 to 16 billion m3

onset.what: Zambia begins 8 hours a day of load-shedding

crises.peak: Lake at 475.91 m, 2.89% usable, on 11 Dec 2024; Kariba North generation halted about 14 Sep 2024
costs: IMF cut Zambia's 2024 growth forecast from 4.7% to 1.2%, citing power shortfalls [P]
Emergency imports and diesel at 17-26 US cents/kWh: about $51M a month for 300 MW (ZESCO filing) [P]
Load-shedding reported up to 21 hours a day [N]

sources.title: ZESCO tariff application to ERB, Jul 2024

notes: Dates marked approx. are from news reports without an exact official date.
